work_or_witness: The Last Unicorn · Chapter 1, PDF page 10, opening description and “Unicorns are immortal”; PDF page 18, butterfly's “unicorn” etymology
literal_gloss: one-horned; the butterfly supplies an in-text Latin etymology
definition: The opening calls its central but unnamed figure “the unicorn.” It describes unicorns as immortal, magical, usually solitary forest-dwellers, and distinguishes this figure's appearance from a horned horse. The butterfly later recites an etymological gloss for “unicorn.”
cultural_caution: A common noun and creature category is not a stable proper name. No unnamed unicorn is converted into a character node, and no generic race/species taxonomy, gender identity, combat class, healing power, or equivalence to other-universe unicorns is inferred.

canonical_term: seeing a unicorn as a white mare
